messages.subject: a problem with item_response.stan (ARM chapter 19)
parts:
Dear List,

I am trying to get a good grip on estimating item-response models with Stan but I have run into some difficulties.
When I try to run the example code item_response.stan (arm chapter 19), I get the following error:

error in call to assign; require matching dimensions, but found arg1(rows=100,cols=1); arg2(rows=4000,cols=1)Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

I have added a file I used to simulate data as well as the stan file which is available online.

I wonder whether this might be the problem: (line 35 of the stan code)
b_hat_raw <- 100 * b_0_raw + d_raw * x;

Here we want to assign something with length N (line 7: vector[N] x;)  to a container of length K (line 25: vector[K] b_hat_raw;).

Kind regards, Louis

PS: Related to this issue: If someone has some experience with item-response modeling in Stan and would not mind me asking some questions directly, feel free to drop me a line.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] a problem with item_response.stan (ARM chapter 19)
parts:
Thanks for the report. That's definitely a bug in the
coding of that model for exactly the reason you state.

The bigger problem is that the model was too literally translated
from BUGS and it won't work in Stan as written (and we're not
convinced the BUGS models actually worked, either). The problem
is with unidentified models as explained in the problematic posteriors
chapter of the manual. It stems from Andrew's trick in his
book with Jennifer of using a parameterization
with an improper posterior and then trying to normalize the draws.
This won't work in Stan because Stan's too efficient at trying
to explore that improper posterior --- that is, Stan will let you
know you're trying to fit an improper posterior. This is discussed
in the manual.

So we have to redo the example model so that it works. We're
taking a pass through all the ARM models but hadn't gotten that
far yet. Here's the issue to track:

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/issues/5

We've done a fair bit of item-response modeling and
are going to be writing more as part of our IES grant.
Andrew wants us to change all the priors in all of these
models to be more informative and get rid of the uniform
vague priors on standard deviation.

I'm attaching a working item-response model and an R program
to simulate from it. It's a little more complicated in that it
has hierarchical school-level effects. And it still uses those
uniform priors on standard deviations (we'd probably now
use a cauchy(0,2.5) prior with only a lower=0 constraint).

- Bob
